channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Thiago Ávila chega em SP nesta 2ª feira após prisão em Israel
item.description: Brazilian Palestinian rights activist Thiago Ávila arrived in São Paulo on Monday (May 11, 2026) after being deported from Israel, where he had been detained since April 29 for participating in the Global Sumud Flotilla humanitarian mission to Gaza. He was intercepted in international waters, subjected to prolonged interrogations by Israeli intelligence services using alleged coercive methods and threats, and only released following pressure from President Lula, who called his detention 'unjustifiable'.

item.title: 41,2% dos brasileiros dizem conviver com o crime organizado
item.description: The "Fear of Crime and Elections 2026" report reveals that 41.2% of Brazilians aged 16 or older recognize the presence of organized criminal groups in their neighborhoods, equivalent to 68.7 million people. Conducted by Datafolha for the Brazilian Forum of Public Security, the study shows that organized crime has expanded beyond major capitals through territorial diffusion, affecting the routines of 57% of the population and increasing victimization rates to 51.1% in areas dominated by criminal factions.

item.title: Investigadores revisitam traumas da Lava-Jato para tentar não repetir erros no caso Master
item.description: The lawyer for Daniel Vorcaro, José Luís Oliveira Lima (Juca), met with TSE Minister Floriano de Azevedo Marques, an ally of Alexandre de Moraes, at a Brasília hotel last Wednesday (6) to discuss legal strategies aimed at avoiding the investigative mistakes of Operation Lava-Jato in the Master case.

item.title: Governo deve lançar programa contra o crime organizado nesta semana
item.description: The federal government is set to launch the 'Brazil Against Organized Crime' program next Tuesday (12), with R$ 11 billion in funding (R$ 1 billion from the budget and R$ 10 billion via BNDES loan). The initiative includes axes such as arms trafficking combat, financial suffocation of organized crime, increased homicide clearance rates, and prison security upgrades, including cell phone blockers and modern X-ray equipment. Implementation depends on state adherence, which would grant access to federal funds.

item.title: Nunes Marques e Mendonça assumem TSE, abrindo nova fase da Corte
item.description: Kassio Nunes Marques assumes the presidency of the TSE in an anticipated succession from Cármen Lúcia, with a mandate until May 2028, to be followed by André Mendonça until 2030. Both were appointed by Jair Bolsonaro and are expected to oversee the 2026 and 2028 elections with a profile of discretion and impartiality. Cármen Lúcia’s departure opens the seat for Dias Toffoli to return to the TSE, marking a shift in the Court’s composition, which will not have another woman in the presidency until at least 2042.

item.title: Lula deve anunciar quase R$ 1 bilhão em investimentos na Segurança Pública nesta semana
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is set to announce this week a nearly R$1 billion investment package for public security actions, focusing on combating organized crime, arms trafficking, and improving the prison system. The funds will be allocated to the National Public Security Fund and the National Penitentiary Fund via a decree and four ordinances. The announcement comes amid growing pressure for concrete results in security, especially ahead of the 2026 elections and in the context of international cooperation against organized financial crime.

item.title: Presidenciáveis da direita sobem tom contra Moraes por barrar Lei da Dosimetria, e oposição mira retomar debate da anistia
item.description: Right-wing presidential contenders, including Flávio Bolsonaro, Romeu Zema, and Ronaldo Caiado, intensified criticism of Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes after the STF suspended the Dosimetry Law, which reduced sentences for January 8 convicts. The opposition is pushing for a constitutional amendment to grant broad amnesty to those involved in the riot, while the PT, PV, and PCdoB defend the Court’s decision. Zema accused Moraes of 'overrunning Congress' and considering himself 'untouchable'.

item.title: Neymar, Rayan, Pedro: jogadores que ainda buscam vaga na Copa tentam sprint final para convencer Ancelotti
item.description: With just one week left until Brazil's 2026 World Cup squad announcement, players like Neymar, Rayan, Igor Jesus, João Pedro, and Pedro are pushing for final spots in Carlo Ancelotti's list. Some are showcasing form in decisive Premier League and FA Cup matches, while others face uncertainty due to injuries or recent fitness concerns. The roster will be revealed on the 18th at the Museum of Tomorrow in Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: Lula caminha na Granja do Torto 16 dias após cirurgia
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was seen walking at the Granja do Torto residence 16 days after undergoing surgery to remove a basal cell carcinoma from his scalp. The procedure, performed on April 24 at the Sírio-Libanês Hospital, was deemed minor with no subsequent restrictions. Lula also received a corticosteroid injection in his right thumb to treat tendinitis, both procedures approved by medical officials.

item.title: Bolsonarista publica vídeo bebendo detergente Ypê
item.description: A Bolsonaro supporter published a video drinking Ypê detergent while making obscene gestures toward PT supporters. The video spreads as a meme on social media, tied to unsubstantiated claims that Lula’s government is using Anvisa to persecute the company, whose owners backed Bolsonaro in 2022. Anvisa had ordered a product recall on May 7 due to manufacturing practice failures, a preventive measure to avoid bacterial contamination risk.

item.title: 68 milhões de brasileiros moram em áreas com presença de facções e milícias, aponta pesquisa
item.description: A survey by the Brazilian Forum of Public Safety and Datafolha finds that 68 million Brazilians (41% of the population) perceive the presence of criminal factions and militias in their neighborhoods, with nearly half describing their activity as 'visible' or 'very visible'. The impact extends beyond fear, affecting daily routines, mobility, and consumption, as organized crime shapes neighborhood rules and exerts territorial control, primarily through the PCC, Red Command, and dozens of other groups.

item.title: Golpes digitais preocupam 83% da população, aponta levantamento
item.description: A survey by the Brazilian Forum of Public Safety in partnership with Datafolha shows that 83.2% of Brazilians fear becoming victims of digital scams, making it the top concern, technically tied with fear of armed robbery (82.3%) and being killed during an assault (80.7%). The report also states that digital scams were the most frequent crime experienced in the last 12 months, affecting 15.8% of the population — approximately 26.3 million people — with notable use of fake automatic CNH renewal as bait.

item.title: Medo da violência altera a rotina de 57% dos brasileiros e afeta mais mulheres e população de baixa renda, diz pesquisa
item.description: A survey by the Brazilian Forum on Public Security and Datafolha shows that 57% of Brazilians changed their routines due to fear of violence in the past 12 months, with 96.2% reporting fear of at least one violent situation. Common adaptations include altering usual routes (36.5%), avoiding going out at night (35.6%), and not carrying cellphones due to robbery fears (33.5%). The burden falls disproportionately on women and low-income populations (classes D/E), who experience more intense and widespread fear, particularly regarding sexual aggression and patrimonial vulnerability.

item.title: 41% dos brasileiros afirmam conviver com o crime organizado no bairro onde moram
item.description: 41.2% of Brazilians aged 16 or older report living with the presence of organized crime in their neighborhoods, according to a report by the Brazilian Forum of Public Security. This equals 68.7 million people, with higher perception in state capitals (55.9%) and spread even to interior cities (34.1%). The influence of these groups on local rules of coexistence is acknowledged by 61.4% of those who recognize them, reflecting a 'criminal governance' and a 'duopoly of violence' alongside the State.

item.title: Às vésperas da eleição, 6 a cada 10 brasileiros têm medo de sofrer agressões por opção política
item.description: 60% of Brazilians fear physical aggression due to their political choices, a level of concern similar to four years ago. The study by the Brazilian Forum of Public Security and Datafolha shows women, poorer classes (D and E), and residents in areas with organized crime presence are most affected, with 2.2% reporting having suffered political violence in the last 12 months.

item.title: Pesquisa indica subnotificação generalizada de roubos de celular e golpes na internet
item.description: A Datafolha survey indicates that underreporting of cellphone theft and internet fraud in Brazil may exceed 90%, with approximately 26.3 million people affected by digital scams and 13.9 million by cellphone robbery/theft in the last 12 months—far above official figures of 2.1 million and 918,000, respectively. Fear of these crimes is widespread, with 96% of respondents expressing concern about becoming victims, particularly of online scams, prompting calls for specific policy proposals from candidates in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Erika e Sâmia acionam órgãos contra Tarcísio após ação da PM na USP
item.description: Federal deputies Erika Hilton and Sâmia Bomfim (PSOL-SP) have filed complaints with the São Paulo State Prosecutor's Office, the Military Police Corregedor, and the Public Ministry against Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, the Military Police, and USP's rectorate following a violent police operation that cleared the university's rectorate occupied by students. They condemned the use of force, lack of judicial authorization, and alleged collusion between police and university authorities, asserting the students' constitutional right to protest.

item.title: Deputado bolsonarista envia ofício para a CBF para pedir a convocação de Neymar para a Copa do Mundo
item.description: Federal deputy Hélio Lopes (PL-RJ) sent an official letter to the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) requesting the call-up of Neymar Jr. for the World Cup, describing him as Brazil’s all-time top scorer and a national symbol of talent and hope, while stating he does not intend to interfere technically in team selections. The request was shared on social media, where Lopes also urged coach Carlo Ancelotti and the CBF to 'call Neymar'. Datafolha data reveals 62% of Flávio Bolsonaro supporters back the call-up, compared to 46% of Lula supporters, with 53% of the general public in favor.

item.title: PT, PCdoB e PV apresentam ação ao STF para derrubar dosimetria que beneficia Bolsonaro
item.description: The PT, PCdoB, and PV, through the Hope Brazil Federation, filed an action with the STF to declare the Dosimetry Law unconstitutional, which reduces sentences for those convicted in the January 8 attacks, including former President Jair Bolsonaro. They also request a precautionary measure to immediately suspend the law’s application, arguing it unfairly benefits participants in the anti-democratic events.

item.title: Dosimetria: Oposição prepara ofensiva contra Moraes no Congresso
item.description: The PL is preparing an offensive in Congress against Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes following the suspension of the Dosimetry Law for those convicted in the January 8 attacks. The party plans to pressure the heads of the Chamber and Senate to advance a PEC against unilateral court decisions and an amnesty bill, while also seeking to revive an impeachment request against Moraes, which, according to the PL Senate leader, already has over 42 signatures — more than half the Senate.

item.title: STF dá prazo de cinco dias para Moro responder a processo de calúnia contra Gilmar Mendes
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Cármen Lúcia has given Senator Sergio Moro five days to submit his preliminary defense in a slander case filed against Justice Gilmar Mendes, following Moro’s October 2023 video claim that a habeas corpus could be 'bought' from Mendes. The First Chamber of the STF previously rejected Moro’s appeals and maintained him as a defendant, with the PGR asserting he intended to damage Mendes’s honor. Moro is running for governor of Paraná in 2026 as the PL candidate, allied with Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential bid.

item.title: Na despedida de Hulk, Atlético-MG cede o empate ao Botafogo no fim e freia reação no
item.description: Atlético-MG drew 1-1 with Botafogo in stoppage time after leading through Cassierra’s 23rd-minute goal. Artur Cabral equalized in the 44th minute of the second half, halting Atlético-MG’s Brazilian Serie A resurgence as both teams remain on 18 points. The match featured an emotional farewell to club idol Hulk, who is departing for Fluminense and was honored with a standing ovation, 3D mosaic, flags, and institutional video by the fans.

item.title: Flávio sem Ciro Nogueira seria como um Piu-Piu sem o Frajola
item.description: The analyst suggests that Flávio Bolsonaro is attempting to distance himself from Senator Ciro Nogueira, but this effort raises voter skepticism, as it appears to be more a convenient strategy than a genuine break. The comparison to 'Piu-Piu without Frajola' implies Flávio loses political meaning without Ciro’s support, indicating dependence and lack of autonomy. The narrative indicates that truth matters less than convenience for Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign.

item.title: MPF abre investigação sobre omissão climática do governo Lula
item.description: The Federal Public Ministry (MPF) has opened an investigation into alleged misappropriation of federal funds allocated for COP 30 infrastructure projects in Pará, as well as the Lula government’s alleged omission in responding to climate emergencies and their impacts on fundamental rights such as health, housing, and education for vulnerable groups. The inquiry focuses on irregularities in resource use and governmental inaction amid the climate crisis.

item.title: Ciro Nogueira vira mais uma figurinha no organograma petista do ‘bolsomaster’
item.description: A Federal Police conducted a search and seizure at the home of Senator Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI), which bolstered the PT's strategy to link the Banco Master scheme to the Bolsonaro family, using the term 'bolsomaster' to damage the image of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president in 2026. Despite accusations by Deputy Paulo Pimenta, the government leader in the Chamber, there is no evidence or investigation implicating Flávio Bolsonaro or former President Jair Bolsonaro in the case.

item.title: Haddad diz que “extrema-direita” domina debate público
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) warned that the far-right dominates public discourse with shallow discourses on social media, while the left struggles to expand its dialogue and political formation, especially before a largely conservative Congress. He advocated for the Perseu Abramo Foundation to act as a center of theoretical reflection and intellectual formation for the PT, expanding access to classic and contemporary bibliography. Haddad also noted that the left has lost ground on digital platforms due to the technological dominance of conservative groups and urged Brazil to debate AI development models inspired by the U.S. and China.

item.title: Oposição fala em ressuscitar "PEC da Anistia" no Congresso, após Moraes suspender Lei da Dosimetria
item.description: The suspension of the Dosimetry Law by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes prompted opposition lawmakers to threaten a Constitutional Amendment Proposal (PEC) granting broad amnesty to those convicted of the January 8 attacks. Government allies welcomed the decision, while Bolsonaro allies denounced it as an affront to legislative sovereignty. The initiative faces procedural hurdles and requires high legislative consensus to succeed.

item.title: Bate-boca por chapa ao Senado em SP contrapõe Salles e Constantino a Eduardo Bolsonaro e Mário Frias
item.description: The PL's Senate pre-candidacy dispute in SP has pitted Ricardo Salles and Rodrigo Constantino against Eduardo Bolsonaro, Mário Frias, and Gil Diniz over the endorsement of André do Prado. Salles accused Eduardo of submitting to Valdemar Costa Neto's 'physiological centrão,' while Eduardo countered that Salles 'tucked his tail between his legs' by avoiding confrontation with the STF. The exchange highlights ideological fractures within São Paulo's bolsonarist right.

item.title: PT, PV e PCdoB acionam STF contra Lei da Dosimetria, que prevê redução de penas dos condenados do 8/1
item.description: The PT, PV, and PCdoB parties filed an ADI with the STF challenging the Dosimetry Law, which reduces sentences for those convicted in the January 8 attacks, arguing it is unconstitutional and risks releasing individuals involved in a plot against democracy. They seek a precautionary measure to suspend the law, accusing Congress of partially overturning the presidential veto to benefit Bolsonaro's allies. Minister Alexandre de Moraes had previously suspended the law's application in an individual ruling.

item.title: Ypê teve produtos suspensos “porque apoiou Bolsonaro”, diz Adrilles
item.description: São Paulo city councilor Adrilles Jorge (União) claimed that Anvisa's suspension of Ypê products was politically motivated, alleging the company supported Bolsonaro. He cited donations totaling R$ 1 million from the Beira family, Ypê's controllers, to Bolsonaro's 2022 campaign. The move sparked social media defense campaigns by Lula opposition figures, accusing the government of weaponizing Anvisa to punish companies based on political affiliations.

item.title: Zema tem dificuldades em MG e é pressionado pelo PL a desistir para ajudar sucessor no Estado
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) is struggling in Minas Gerais with only 11% of first-round presidential vote intentions, behind Lula (32%) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL, 27%). Although he leads in a simulated second-round matchup against Lula (38% to 37%), his weak performance in the state he governed for seven years is attributed to declining approval, end-of-cycle fatigue, and national polarization, prompting pressure from the PL for him to step aside to support a state successor.

item.title: Neoenergia investirá R$ 50 bilhões em distribuidoras em 5 anos
item.description: Neoenergia announced R$ 50 billion in investments for its electricity distributors between 2026 and 2030, in a ceremony in Brasília attended by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Minister Alexandre Silveira. The amount represents an 82% increase over the previous period and will be allocated to infrastructure expansion (46%), modernization and digitalization (40%), and loss reduction and operational support (14%). The early renewal of concessions for Neoenergia Coelba, Cosern, Elektro and Pernambuco was signed the same day.

item.title: Estudo mostra distância entre indígenas e participação eleitoral
item.description: The study shows that although 70% of Brazil's Indigenous population is 15 years or older and eligible to vote, only 15% self-declare as Indigenous voters before the TSE. The largest gap is among youth aged 15–19, with only 32.6% electoral coverage, and there is a slight overrepresentation of women in the Indigenous electorate compared to the general Indigenous population.

item.title: Michelle Bolsonaro sai em defesa da Ypê após suspensão da Anvisa; veja foto
item.description: Former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro posted an Instagram story showing her holding a Ypê detergent in support of the company after Anvisa suspended production of certain batches due to potential microbial contamination. Bolsonaro allies framed the move as political persecution by the Lula government, particularly after it was revealed that the Beira family, owners of Ypê, donated to Bolsonaro’s 2022 campaign. The incident reignited a pattern of bolsonarist mobilization against companies perceived as targets of government retaliation, similar to the backlash against Havaianas in December 2023.

item.title: Renan Santos é o pré-candidato que mais cresce no TikTok
item.description: Renan Santos, the pre-candidate for presidency from the Missão party, led proportional follower growth on social media in April 2026, with a 44.7% increase on TikTok (from 218.5k to 316.2k followers) and 36.9% overall growth across monitored platforms, reaching 1.7 million followers. Despite strong digital momentum, he holds only 1.5% voting intention in the latest Meia/Ideia poll from May 2026. His platform focuses on fighting organized crime, reducing the state size, privatizing public companies, and revising Bolsa Família.

item.title: Petra Costa fala de indicada ao Emmy por direção de ‘Apocalipse nos Trópicos’
item.description: Brazilian filmmaker Petra Costa has been nominated for the 2026 News & Documentary Emmy Awards in the Best Documentary Direction category for her film 'Apocalipse nos Trópicos'. The documentary investigates the intersection of religion, power, and politics in Brazil, focusing on the growing influence of evangelical leaders in national politics, with access to figures such as Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Silas Malafaia. Costa draws a parallel between Brazil’s current political-religious landscape and the rise of the Moral Majority in the U.S. during the 1970s and 80s, comparing Silas Malafaia’s influence on Bolsonaro to Billy Graham’s influence on Nixon.

item.title: Dilema do STF
item.description: The crisis of the Supreme Federal Court operates on two levels: one involving individual conduct such as conflicts of interest and corruption suspicions, and another, deeper, concerning the institution’s institutional behavior and relationship with the other branches of government. The text argues the issue extends beyond personal failings to threaten the Court’s legitimacy as an institution.

item.title: Funk da Pilili exorciza mascote do TSE
item.description: The TSE's mascot Pilili, launched to celebrate 30 years of electronic voting, was parodied in a video by the Canta Direita profile using a funk version of DJ Marlboro's 'Atoladinha'. In the animation, Pilili makes the 'L' gesture associated with Lula, which critics interpreted as a symbolic exorcism of the figure. The video went viral, sparking debate about AI and political satire in Brazil.

item.title: Neymar: a reta final no Santos por uma vaga na seleção brasileira de Ancelotti
item.description: Neymar is in a decisive final stretch with Santos to secure a spot in Brazil's 2026 World Cup squad under coach Carlo Ancelotti, with only three matches remaining before the announcement. Ancelotti has stated he will only select Neymar if he reaches 100% physical fitness following a prolonged injury period. The player views the World Cup as his 'last mission' in football and is training intensely, despite expressing disappointment over not being called up for recent friendlies.

item.title: Por que as campanhas de Flávio e Lula estão de olho em jovens e mulheres para vencer a eleição
item.description: The campaigns of Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula are targeting young voters (16-34) and women, identified as the most likely to change their vote before October. Genial/Quaest data shows 52% of undecided voters are young and 49% are women, with up to 81% of Romeu Zema’s supporters still open to shifting allegiance. The strategy focuses on economic issues and Flávio’s relatively youthful, less polarizing image to attract voters alienated by his father’s legacy.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro publicam mensagens de Dia das Mães com acenos ao eleitorado feminino
item.description: President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a pre-candidate for president, posted Mother's Day messages on social media, highlighting tributes to women as a strategy to attract the female electorate, a key demographic in the 2026 elections. Both sought to associate their images with values of care and recognition of women, in a conciliatory yet political tone.

item.title: STF ganha protagonismo na política e vira tema de campanha eleitoral; veja propostas dos presidenciáveis
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) has become a central theme in the 2026 presidential pre-campaign, with candidates proposing judiciary reforms such as fixed terms for justices, a new selection process, and the end of monocratic decisions. Ministers like Flávio Dino and Edson Fachin are also advocating internal reforms, including competency review and a code of ethics. Experts note the STF’s increased political prominence stems from congressional inaction on constitutional issues, prompting the Court to fill legislative gaps.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro acenam ao eleitorado feminino em mensagem de dia das mães
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro used Mother's Day to honor women on social media, aiming to connect with the female electorate, which constitutes 52.8% of Brazil's voters. Lula recalled his mother, Dona Lindu, and praised the courage of millions of Brazilian women, while Bolsonaro personalized his message around his wife and mother, emphasizing maternal perseverance. Polls show Lula leading among women with 43% voting intention, compared to Bolsonaro's 32%, highlighting the strategic importance of this demographic in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Zema e Flávio são os pré-candidatos com mais interações nas redes
item.description: Romeu Zema and Flávio Bolsonaro lead social media interactions among presidential pre-candidates in April, with 26.0 and 24.4 million engagements, respectively. Lula ranks third with 17.1 million. Zema’s engagement spiked after a clash with Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes, while Bolsonaro leads in average engagement per post at 72,000.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro anuncia a ‘conta-gotas’ itens de seu programa de governo
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) has been gradually unveiling items of his government program through speeches and social media, without formal details, focusing on economy, security, foreign policy, and environment. Key proposals include ending new indigenous land demarcations, streamlining environmental licensing for infrastructure like the Ferrogrão railway, abolishing taxes such as the 'blusinhas' tax, lowering the age of criminal responsibility to 16 (14 for serious crimes), granting amnesty to those convicted for the January 8 events, creating an integrated digital government system, and enforcing fiscal discipline with Central Bank independence.

item.title: “O Pix é do Bolsonaro, o Master é do Lula”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro attended a PL event in Santa Catarina wearing a t-shirt with the slogan 'The Pix is Bolsonaro's, the Master is Lula's'. He has been using slogan-bearing t-shirts as part of his pre-presidential campaign, replacing the caps previously used. The move reinforces the PL's communication strategy of contrasting Bolsonaro and Lula on economic and symbolic themes.

item.title: Carlos Bolsonaro chora ao falar que Eduardo talvez não volte ao Brasil
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro cried while stating that his brother Eduardo Bolsonaro may never return to Brazil due to self-exile in the U.S. since 2025, citing political persecution and risk of arrest. He also praised Flávio Bolsonaro for his alleged courage in running for president and for acknowledging their father Jair Bolsonaro’s mistakes, claiming Flávio would not repeat them. The text also references PL events in Santa Catarina and Flávio’s remarks on various political topics.

item.title: Carta aberta ao Presidente Lula
item.description: Orlando Silva urges President Lula to support PEC 27, which institutionalizes historical reparations for slavery in Brazil through the National Fund for Economic Reparation and Racial Equality Promotion, allocating R$ 1 billion annually over 20 years. He emphasizes that despite its modest financial impact, the proposal is a significant symbolic and concrete step to combat structural racism, acknowledging the state’s responsibility for the legacy of incomplete abolition.

item.title: Em tom eleitoral, Flávio faz vídeo de Dia das Mães: “Carregam 2 mundos”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) posted a Mother's Day video in which he praised women and mothers, stating that 'being a woman and being a mother is carrying two worlds within one body'. He emphasized mothers' strength, resilience, and unconditional love, noting many act alone and without recognition yet transform lives. The video was released as part of his 2026 presidential pre-campaign.

item.title: Lula, Flávio e políticos compartilham mensagens de Dia das Mães
item.description: Politicians from different ideological spectrums, including Lula (PT), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) and others, used social media on Mother's Day 2026 to honor Brazilian mothers, mixing personal messages, religious references and praise for maternal dedication. Flávio Bolsonaro also shared a video with an electoral tone, highlighting his presidential pre-candidacy.
